findings.claim: Robert Merton, writing in Social Theory and Social Structure (1938, enlarged 1968), developed Durkheim's concept of anomie into a systematic theory of crime.
findings.truth: Merton set out strain theory in his 1938 journal article 'Social Structure and Anomie' (American Sociological Review). Social Theory and Social Structure is a later book (first published 1949; revised 1957; enlarged 1968). The title and the 1938 date do not belong together.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Strain theory (sociology): 'Robert K. Merton first introduced strain theory in 1938 in the article Social Structure and Anomie, published in the American Sociological Review'; the same source dates the revised Social Theory and Social Structure to 1957.

findings.claim: Cannabis possession is permitted for recreational use under certain conditions in the Netherlands but remains a criminal offence in England and Wales.
findings.truth: Cannabis possession is not permitted in the Netherlands. It remains illegal under the Opium Act; Dutch policy (gedoogbeleid) directs prosecutors not to pursue small amounts for personal use. The cross-cultural point survives, but as a difference in enforcement, not in the law.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Drug policy of the Netherlands: 'recreational use, possession and trade of non-medicinal drugs described by the Opium Law are all technically illegal under Dutch law'; possession of up to 5 grams is typically not prosecuted.

findings.claim: Cannabis possession is permitted under certain conditions in the Netherlands but is a criminal offence in England and Wales.
findings.truth: Same error as F1 in flashcard form. Replaced with an example where the law itself, not the enforcement policy, differs by place: alcohol.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Drug policy of the Netherlands (as F2).

findings.claim: On a 12-mark Evaluate question, examiners reward students who present at least two named sociological perspectives in detail...
findings.truth: Fabricated examiner claim. The spec publishes no statement of what examiners reward. The advice itself is sound and is kept; the appeal to examiners is removed.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md section 3.1 gives only the AO weightings (AO1 40 / AO2 40 / AO3 20); no examiner commentary is printed.

findings.claim: women are significantly underrepresented as victims of property crime but overrepresented as victims of domestic violence and sexual assault
findings.truth: No source supports the first clause. Household property crime in the Crime Survey for England and Wales is counted per household, so it carries no sex of victim, and for personal theft women are not under-represented. The second clause is correct and is kept.
findings.evidence: ONS Crime Survey for England and Wales methodology: burglary, vehicle crime and criminal damage are household offences recorded at household level; only personal crimes carry victim characteristics.

findings.claim: White-collar and corporate crime committed in private settings (online fraud, insider trading, benefit fraud by corporations)
findings.truth: Benefit fraud is claiming state benefits dishonestly. It is committed by individual claimants, not corporations, and lessons 2 and 3 of this unit correctly list it as a working-class offence that the police do pursue. The example contradicts the unit and the concept.
findings.evidence: Internal contradiction with L02 (Marxist view) and L03, which both list benefit fraud among the working-class offences that enforcement targets; gov.uk defines benefit fraud as a claimant offence.

findings.claim: Match each sampling method to the research situation where it is most appropriate: [Snowball sample / Stratified sample / Pilot study]
findings.truth: A pilot study is not a sampling method. The stem teaches a category error in a lesson whose whole point is the design sequence. The three pairings themselves are correct, so only the stem needs changing.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md 7.1 lists 'use of pilot study' and 'selection of sampling techniques' as separate stages of research design.

findings.claim: Your exam includes a section on applied methods of sociological enquiry.
findings.truth: The spec does not print a section structure. The written exam is 1 hour 45 minutes, 100 marks, and carries a mix of short-answer, structured and extended-response questions, all compulsory, across stratification, crime and deviance and applied methods. Applied methods is a topic area, not a named section.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md 2.2: 'Written examination: 1 hour 45 minutes, 50% of qualification, 100 marks... A written assessment with a mix of short answer, structured questions and extended-response questions, all compulsory.'

findings.claim: The mark scheme asks how each would be addressed in the context of the specific study.
findings.truth: Invented mark-scheme claim. The requirement to propose strategies comes from the spec content, not from a quoted mark scheme.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md 4.5: 'strategies used by sociologists to address issues'.

findings.claim: Applied methods questions are the most commonly under-answered part of the applied research paper.
findings.truth: There is no separate applied research paper. Applied methods is examined inside the same 1 hour 45 minute written exam as social stratification and crime and deviance.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md 2.2 lists the three topic areas of the one written exam: social differentiation and stratification; crime and deviance; applied methods of sociological enquiry.

findings.claim: the 18-24 age group has the highest prosecution rate, followed closely by the 10-17 group
findings.truth: Recomputed from the lesson's own worked table: 18-24 = 22.7, 10-17 = 15.2. The gap is 7.5 per 1,000, so the 10-17 rate is 33% below the 18-24 rate. That is not 'closely'. The lesson elsewhere warns students not to over-state differences, so the model description must be accurate.
findings.evidence: Recomputation: (22.7 - 15.2) / 22.7 = 0.330. Every other figure in the worked table checks out: 22.7 is the highest, 4.1 the lowest, and the fall after age 25 (10.8, then 4.1) is correctly described.

findings.claim: Presenting competing interpretations is what the mark scheme rewards.
findings.truth: Invented mark-scheme claim. The point stands as advice about a strong answer; the appeal to a mark scheme does not.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md prints no mark-scheme wording.

findings.claim: The data interpretation section of your exam rewards students who follow a clear sequence...
findings.truth: Two problems in one clause: the exam has no printed data interpretation section, and the claim about what the exam rewards is fabricated. The sequence itself is good advice and is kept.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md 2.2 (no section structure printed) and 7.2 (interpreting graphs, diagrams, charts and tables is required content, not a named section).

findings.claim: Mark schemes across all eight lessons use the band names Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging, and six exam tips refer to reaching 'the Mastering tier'.
findings.truth: These are invented band labels written as though they were the board's. The house vocabulary is Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band. The labels are not on the validator's banned list, so nothing fails, but they read as board wording. Options: (a) rename across all 16 mark schemes and 6 exam tips in this unit; (b) leave them and handle the naming as a subject-wide sweep. This is a bulk rename, not a fact fix, so it is not in _edits.json.
findings.evidence: scripts/_retrofc/CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md, copyright distancing and banned-strings rules.
findings.ruling: NOTE: Mastering/Secure/Developing/Emerging band names left for the programme-wide band-ladder sweep.

findings.claim: The lesson gives two different design sequences. The Key Fact at n7 runs 'aim - hypothesis - method choice - sampling - pilot study - data collection - analysis'. The Key Fact at n26 gives six stages ending in ethical issues, with no analysis step.
findings.truth: Spec 7.1 lists analysis of data as required content, and the two lists in this one lesson contradict each other. Options: (a) make the framework seven stages, add analysis of data, and align both lists; (b) leave, since neither list is factually wrong on its own. Recommendation: (a) - a student revising 'the six stages' meets two different lists in one lesson. Rewriting a framework across two Key Facts is beyond a surgical fix, so it is left for a ruling.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md 7.1: choosing a research area; establishing an aim and/or hypothesis; choosing a method; use of pilot study; selection of sampling techniques; analysis of data; usefulness of mixed methods approach.
findings.ruling: NOTE: two Key Fact design sequences conflict and omit 'analysis of data' - a framework rewrite across two Key Facts, recorded for a later authoring pass.

findings.claim: Question tariffs of 1, 2, 3, 4, 9 and 12 marks with the command words Define, Identify and Describe, Describe, Discuss and Evaluate appear across all eight lessons.
findings.truth: The spec prints no question ladder, so these tariffs cannot be verified. None of them contradicts or is impossible against the printed facts: 1 hour 45 minutes, 100 marks, 50% of the qualification, AO1 40 / AO2 40 / AO3 20, research methods at least 15% of marks. No 20-mark or 25-mark question, no SPaG marks and no other board's paper names appear anywhere in the unit.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md 2.2 and 3.1.

findings.claim: Police-recorded crime... published by the Home Office as a measure of crime trends.
findings.truth: The headline crime statistics for England and Wales have been published by the Office for National Statistics since April 2012, when responsibility transferred from the Home Office. The Home Office does still publish the police recorded crime open data tables, so the wording is defensible and is left alone.
findings.evidence: ONS Crime in England and Wales bulletin series; Home Office police recorded crime and outcomes open data tables.

findings.claim: The Crime Survey for England and Wales (CSEW) was established in 1982.
findings.truth: Correct as a date for the survey series, which first ran in 1982. It was called the British Crime Survey until April 2012, when it was renamed the Crime Survey for England and Wales. Not worth an edit at GCSE, but a student who meets 'British Crime Survey' in a source should know it is the same survey.
findings.evidence: ONS Crime Survey for England and Wales background notes.

findings.claim: Primary deviance and secondary deviance are introduced in the section on Becker.
findings.truth: The terms are Edwin Lemert's (Social Pathology, 1951). The lesson does not attribute them to Becker, so nothing is wrong, but they sit under a Becker heading. The spec names only Becker here, so no edit.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/sociology-C200QS.md 6.4: 'self-fulfilling prophecy, including the work of Becker and the deviant career'.

findings.claim: Which sociological perspective argues that official crime statistics reflect policing priorities rather than true levels of offending? Key: Interactionism. Marxism is also an option.
findings.truth: The lesson's own text separates them: interactionists say the statistics measure policing activity; Marxists say they reflect class power. The key is defensible on that reading, so no edit, but the distractor is close.
findings.evidence: L06 content_html, Sociological Perspectives on Crime Data.

summary: One HIGH error: Merton's strain theory is attributed to Social Theory and Social Structure (1938), collapsing the 1938 journal article into the later book. The rest are a cluster of fabricated examiner and mark-scheme claims and invented exam sections in the two applied-methods lessons, a Dutch cannabis claim that states tolerance as legalisation, an unsupported claim about women as victims of property crime, benefit fraud misfiled as a corporate crime, a pilot study called a sampling method, and one over-stated description of the unit's own worked data table. Every figure in L07 and L08 was recomputed; only the 'followed closely' description failed. All 40 knowledge-check keys are correct, no board name appears in prose, and no banned band or paper code appears.
